title: Ramp energy lab
target: Compare gravitational energy change with measured kinetic energy.
criteria: Measure height vertically and speed at a stated location.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: To calculate a cart’s lost gravitational energy on a ramp, which length is needed?
options: Vertical drop of its center of mass.
cpa.guide: Gravitational energy change depends on vertical height change.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A trial compares energy at release with energy at a marked finish line. Where should final speed be measured?
options: At a different height without adjustment.
cpa.guide: Energy terms must describe the same initial and final states.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A supplied 2 kg cart drops 0.60 m; g = 10 N/kg. What energy is released from gravity?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A supplied trial loses 15 J of gravitational energy and gains 11 J translational plus 2 J rotational energy. What energy remains for other transfers?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A measured ramp energy difference is 0.3 J with estimated uncertainty ±0.6 J. Which conclusion is supported?
options: The difference is consistent with zero within this uncertainty.
The experiment proves exactly 0.3 J was destroyed.
Uncertainty can be ignored because the difference is positive.
cpa.guide: The uncertainty interval includes zero; this does not establish an exact loss or absence of friction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A ramp cart has less translational energy than the gravitational loss predicts. Which investigation is best?
options: Assign the entire difference to destroyed energy.
Change the data until they match.
Include wheel rotation, resistance, sensor uncertainty, and consistent measurement locations.
cpa.guide: Several terms and uncertainties can explain a mismatch; check them explicitly.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
